rows.note: Built like for like rather than compared revenue against FCF. Revenue 5,935,900,000 compounding at 10% for five years gives 9,559,826,309 in FY2031. At a 17.5% steady-state operating margin (this dive's own row-2 case) that is operating income of 1,672,969,604; holding FY2026's own cash-conversion ratio (free cash flow over operating income, 972,400,000 / 1,101,800,000 = 0.8826) gives FY2031 free cash flow of 1,476,489,057, an 8.71% FCF CAGR from the 972,400,000 base. Against the filed 12.29% market-implied ask, the gap is 3.58 percentage points, narrower than the file's own 4.36-point horizon_spread: NOT a real gap by the file's own rule. Stressed at the other end of the operating_margin row's range: holding FY2026's actual elevated margin (18.56%) flat instead of normalizing gives, by construction, a 10.00% FCF CAGR (margin held flat means FCF grows exactly with revenue), a 2.29-point gap, also inside the horizon_spread. Stressed toward the low end of the FY2023-2025 historical margin range (16.56%) gives a 7.52% FCF CAGR, a 4.77-point gap, marginally OUTSIDE the horizon_spread by 0.41 points. The finding does not flip sign across any of these three readings (all say the market wants somewhat more than this dive defends), only whether the SIZE clears the file's own noise bar, and it clears it only at the most bearish of the three margin assumptions examined. This dive reports the range honestly rather than picking the reading that would manufacture a wider gap: the base case (8.71%, 17.5% margin) is inside the noise band, which is why the verdict below is WATCH rather than a confident INVESTABLE call, and why the operating-margin path (whether FY2026's jump holds, partly gives back, or fully reverts) is this dive's single most consequential unresolved input, more so than the revenue growth rate itself.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market prices STERIS off one consolidated growth number (9.38% trailing 3-year revenue CAGR, 18.56% operating margin); it is not distinguishing the Life Sciences segment's much faster capital-equipment growth (+19% Q4 FY2026, +17% Q1 FY2027) that plausibly houses the decontamination/isolator systems this chain link tracks, and it cannot, because STERIS discloses nothing finer than the segment level (9.92% of group revenue) for this business.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: The category of error is conglomerate/segment blindness: a $21.9 billion diversified medical-device and life-sciences equipment maker reports one blended set of growth and margin figures, so a faster-growing product line inside a $588.8 million segment (9.92% of revenue) cannot move the multiple the market assigns to the whole company, even if that product line is genuinely accelerating. This is the opposite failure mode from the crowded, thematically-obvious names this analyst's log has flagged before (VRT, HUBB): here the mechanism is real but structurally too small and too undisclosed to show up in anyone's model, which is also why the chain's own heat map scores this link's crowdedness at only 25/100, the thinnest of the three O1 links promoted on this chain this run.
independence_test.falsification: Stated to prove this dive WRONG, not to confirm it. If Life Sciences capital-equipment growth decelerates back toward the segment's own 8.6% FY2026 organic average (or below the 10% level named in watch_triggers[0]) at the Q2 FY2027 release, expected around early November 2026 and inside review_by, that would show the recent 17-19% prints were order-timing lumpiness on a handful of large capital projects rather than a structural, GLP-1-linked re-acceleration, and this dive's largest_disagreement would not survive contact with the data.

High = $212.29 is the price at which the ask falls to 11.00%, a partial-credit case above the achieved rate but still below both this dive's own 'mine' row (10%) and the market's current 12.29% ask. Both solved by converting enterprise value to price via the file's own net-debt bridge (net debt 1,167,900,000, 97,800,000 shares_used: price = (EV - net_debt) / shares; this bridge reproduces the filed 224.415 exactly at the filed 12.29% ask, confirming the replication is faithful to the filed formula rather than a different model). The zone sits 5.4%-11.8% below the $224.415 reference, shallower than every prior would-buy zone this analyst has drawn (VRT 40.4-44.9%, HUBB 17.6-33.6%, MYRG 53.6-61.5%, ESLT 48.1-59.7% below spot), which this dive treats as an honest consequence of the gap being genuinely thin (net_gap_direction: 2.29-4.79 points, inside or barely outside the 4.36-point horizon_spread) rather than as a shallow zone drawn to manufacture a false close call: a name with a wide, defensible mispricing would earn a deep zone, and this dive has not found one here.
